text:
anya: Heads up — CI e2e shows a big perf regression after yesterday's runtime merge. p90 token-latency jumped ~38% on long-seq workloads. :eyes:
mike: ugh. which merge? any trace/stack?
anya: merge commit `d4f7a2b` (kernel selector rev). CI link: https://ci.internal/reports/2201112222 — summary at top.
perf-ci: perf alert: project=runtime test=e2e_longseq metric=token_latency_p90 baseline=120ms current=165ms delta=+38% (failing since build 4821)
lina: I ran a quick flamegraph locally against a repro harness — seeing spike in compile_worker time and a lot of fresh kernel compilations for small seq lengths. KV cache miss rate also skyrocketed.
ryan: that matches my monitoring. compile_queue depth jumped at the same time the selector started preferring scan-based kernels for mid-range seqs.
mike: can we bisect to confirm the selector change is the culprit?
anya: started bisect this morning, narrowed to `d4f7a2b` -> `d9a3ff0` range. suspect change is the new "scan-first" heuristic that calculates score = src_pref + seq_penalty.
lina: local repro script: `tools/repro/run_longseq --profile` (attached) — outputs: ```
compile_worker: 24.3s
kernel_compile_count: 182
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.42
```
mike: if selector churns picks every request we end up invalidating compiled cache or compiling many micro-variants. That explains the compile storm and high p90.
anya: options: revert the merge, disable new heuristic flag in rollout config, or add a debounce to kernel selection to avoid triggering compile for small deltas. Which do we want for a hotfix?
ryan: revert easiest for immediate mitigation. We should also add a safety gate in the selector to avoid compile on autopick flips unless confidence > 0.9.
lina: I can sketch a debounce patch: add per-model last_pick and only trigger compile if pick changed AND (now - last_pick_ts) > 30s OR request count with new pick > 50.
mike: temporary config toggle: ```json
{"kernel_selector": {"scan_v2": false}}
```
Deploy that to canary first?
anya: yes — will push toggle to canary, watch compile_queue and kv miss. If stable roll to prod. If not, we revert `d4f7a2b`.
perf-ci: note: there are also packaging differences in the merge that bumped compiler flags; include that in bisect path just in case.
mike: assigning tasks — @lina to prepare debounce PR, @anya to push toggle canary + monitor, @ryan to continue bisect for packaging flags.
anya: will post numbers in this thread after canary deploy. :thumbsup:
